mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to higher corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in industrial production suggests increased economic activity, boosting S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by 1% in the last month
failure_condition: Industrial production rises by 1%, but S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment decreases and payroll employment increases, it signals a strong labor market, leading to higher S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment decreases and payroll increases, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in federal funds rate indicates easier monetary policy, boosting equity markets and leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate decreases by 0.1%, but S&P 500 returns are not positive in over 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate increased consumer demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase by 5%, but S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rates signal a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate below 6%, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production and GDP both increase, supply-side growth boosts S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Both industrial production and GDP increase, but S&P 500 returns are not positive in over 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in retail sales indicates strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Retail sales increase by 2%, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.
